text: A lot of the things the sample contains are just what you expect from inexpert writers in general. Repeating the same idea over and over, leaning on stock phrases and concepts, bad structure and infelicitous narrative flow...

I agree that the sample of prose there reads like someone awkwardly imagining a (bad) tv show and transcribing what's on screen into the start of a (bad) novel, but that may be merely a coincidental feature of the writer's particular deficiencies

I don't disagree with the (obvious) idea that people who want to write fiction should read fiction, but I feel like the basic premise of this piece – that there's an "etiology of bad prose," that you can ascribe specific writing tics to someone having "tv brain" – is something I'm very skeptic of.
